I bought two gauges: 0.8mm and 0.3mm both silicone sheathed.•0.3mm²-Very supple and flexible wire, doesn’t drag connectors across the bench.-Soft matte finish silicone sheath that doesn’t char, melt or shrink under a soldering iron. Printed with wire details.-Strips very cleanly and easily. Be careful if using crimp terminals as they can cut into the insulation fairly easily.-Lots of fine tin-plated copper strands. Full 0.3mm².•0.8mm²-All of the above, except the wire is somewhat less flexible. Surprising considering how finely stranded it is. The sheath isn’t as thick compared to the core as the 0.3mm, so maybe there’s just not enough weight.-The retaining holes in the spools are too small, had to drill them out to stop the wire unravelling.•Both come in a cardboard dispenser box which works slightly well. Ended up just taking the spools out.•Both come with a bag of assorted coloured heat shrink of appropriate diameter, a bag of assorted coloured cable ties, and a CAT5 stripping/punchdown tool (why?).
